opportunities.title: Fee + profitability diagnostic
opportunities.wedge: Combine project scope, historical hours, delivery model and client type to flag underpriced work before a proposal is signed.
opportunities.buyer: Architecture firm principal or practice leader.
opportunities.painMoment: We are busy, but the projects are still not producing enough profit and we keep discovering it too late.
opportunities.firstTest: Review 20 completed and proposed projects for one firm and identify fee/scope patterns associated with margin loss.
opportunities.priceHypothesis: US$2k-10k diagnostic or recurring practice analytics
riskNotes: Requires reliable project accounting data.
Firm-specific fee strategy is sensitive.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent match for diagnosis, information design, project-data synthesis and decision support.

evidence.title: AIA: profitability, clients and fees are leading 2026 concerns
evidence.note: 56% cited profitability and new clients/markets as major concerns; 54% cited negotiating appropriate fees.

evidence.title: AIA: negotiating fees has become more challenging
evidence.note: 56% of responding firm leaders said fee negotiation is harder than two years earlier.

opportunities.title: Construction-administration information copilot
opportunities.wedge: Turn RFIs, submittals, site observations, correspondence and change context into one verified project decision trail.
opportunities.buyer: Architecture firm project managers and CA teams.
opportunities.painMoment: The judgment is not the hard part; finding and reconciling the information around it is.
opportunities.firstTest: Shadow one active CA project and automate only the document routing, summarization and decision-log layer.
riskNotes: Professional judgment must remain human-reviewed.
Document provenance and liability matter.
opportunities.fitNote: Near-direct fit for AI orchestration, interaction design and high-stakes document workflows.

evidence.title: AIA: AI can reduce construction-administration burden
evidence.note: AIA describes CA effort as heavily concentrated in managing information around professional judgments.

evidence.title: AIA: project benchmarks are integral to firm decisions
evidence.note: 99% of firms track at least one project benchmark, including hours, fees, budget and construction cost.

opportunities.title: Scope-creep + additional-services detector
opportunities.wedge: Continuously compare contract scope, client requests and project communications to surface uncompensated work before it compounds.
opportunities.buyer: Firm principals, PMs and finance leaders.
opportunities.painMoment: We keep doing extra work because nobody notices the boundary crossed until the job is already over budget.
opportunities.firstTest: Replay three completed projects through a human-reviewed scope classifier and quantify missed additional-service moments.
riskNotes: Contract wording varies substantially.
Needs explainable evidence for every flag.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong semantic-analysis and workflow-intervention fit.

evidence.title: AIA Practice Management Digest: scope creep and profit leakage
evidence.note: AIA practice-management coverage explicitly identifies unchecked scope creep as a predictable source of profit loss.

evidence.title: AIA fee-setting guidance
evidence.note: Fee setting depends on clearly understanding scope, effort, risk and contingencies.

opportunities.title: Project pipeline + staffing capacity planner
opportunities.wedge: Model backlog, signed contracts, pursuit probability, phase-specific hours and skills to show hiring/contractor decisions before capacity breaks.
opportunities.buyer: Architecture practice leader or operations director.
opportunities.painMoment: We can be understaffed and overstaffed within the same quarter because workload arrives by phase, not by headcount.
opportunities.firstTest: Build a spreadsheet-first capacity model for one 20-100 person firm and compare forecasts with actual monthly staffing needs.
riskNotes: Pipeline probabilities are noisy.
Existing ERP/PSA tools may partially address the problem.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong operations/product-modeling fit.

evidence.title: AIA May 2026 staffing survey
evidence.note: 23% of firms reported being understaffed and 15% overstaffed; recruiting remained a problem for 63%.

evidence.title: AIA March 2026 project benchmarks
evidence.note: Firms already track hours by phase, budgets, fees and backlog-relevant measures.

opportunities.title: AI practice governance + verification layer
opportunities.wedge: Define which AI uses are allowed, what source evidence is required and where licensed-professional review must occur.
opportunities.buyer: Architecture firm principal, CIO or risk leader.
opportunities.painMoment: People are already using AI, but the firm has no consistent line between useful acceleration and professional liability.
opportunities.firstTest: Audit AI use in one firm and deploy a lightweight policy plus verification checklist inside three real workflows.
riskNotes: Professional liability implications.
Policy without workflow integration has low value.
opportunities.fitNote: Very strong AI-product governance fit, with architect/risk partner needed for professional standards.

evidence.title: AIA AI Task Force practical guidance
evidence.note: AIA created a dedicated AI Task Force to help firms navigate responsible use and professional judgment.

evidence.title: AIA 2026 business concerns
evidence.note: Effective AI use doubled as a top concern compared with the prior year.

opportunities.title: Prior-authorization workflow automation
opportunities.wedge: Coordinate requirements, evidence, submissions, denials and appeals while keeping every clinical assertion traceable to the chart.
opportunities.buyer: Physician practices, health systems and specialty groups.
opportunities.painMoment: We lose hours every week proving to an insurer that the care we already decided is necessary should be allowed.
opportunities.firstTest: Automate one high-volume authorization class in one specialty and measure staff time, turnaround and approval rate.
riskNotes: HIPAA/security and clinical-safety requirements.
Payer workflows vary and can change.
opportunities.fitNote: Exceptional workflow/AI fit but requires healthcare compliance and clinical partnerships.

evidence.title: AMA 2026 prior authorization survey
evidence.note: Physicians average 40 prior authorizations and 13 physician/staff hours per week; 94% say it contributes to burnout.

evidence.title: AMA prior authorization survey hub
evidence.note: 2026 physician survey finds low confidence that insurer reforms will materially reduce the burden.

opportunities.title: EHR inbox + task-load orchestration
opportunities.wedge: Prioritize messages, results, refill requests and administrative tasks by urgency, ownership and required human judgment.
opportunities.buyer: Medical practices and health-system ambulatory teams.
opportunities.painMoment: The clinical day ends and the second shift of inbox and EHR work begins.
opportunities.firstTest: Observe one clinic team's inbox for two weeks, automate classification/routing only, and measure after-hours EHR time.
riskNotes: Patient safety and protected health information.
Deep EHR integration may be required.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong orchestration/UX fit with mandatory healthcare security and clinical review.

evidence.title: AMA EHR use research
evidence.note: AMA identifies excessive tasks, inbox volume, interruptions and poor interoperability as EHR burdens tied to burnout.

evidence.title: AMA prior authorization burden
evidence.note: Administrative processes continue diverting clinical and staff time from patient care.

opportunities.title: Referral + result loop closure
opportunities.wedge: Track every referral, external result and follow-up obligation until the responsible clinician confirms closure.
opportunities.buyer: Primary-care groups, specialty networks and accountable-care organizations.
opportunities.painMoment: A referral was placed, but nobody can confidently say whether the patient got seen, what happened, or who owns the next step.
opportunities.firstTest: Track one referral pathway manually across two organizations and quantify lost handoffs and staff chase time.
opportunities.priceHypothesis: US$1-5 per tracked episode or enterprise workflow contract
riskNotes: Cross-organization data access is hard.
Missed follow-up can create clinical liability.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent service-design problem but integration and clinical accountability are major barriers.

evidence.title: AMA EHR interoperability and workflow research
evidence.note: Poor interoperability and workflow interruptions remain recognized physician-efficiency problems.

evidence.title: AMA prior authorization patient abandonment evidence
evidence.note: Administrative friction can cause patients to abandon treatment, illustrating the consequence of broken care workflows.

opportunities.title: Practice scheduling + no-show optimizer
opportunities.wedge: Use visit type, patient behavior, staffing and room constraints to fill capacity without making schedules brittle.
opportunities.buyer: Independent practices and outpatient clinics.
opportunities.painMoment: We have a waiting list and still lose clinical capacity to no-shows, gaps and scheduling rules.
opportunities.firstTest: Run a scheduling intervention in one clinic and measure filled slots, wait time and staff rescheduling work.
riskNotes: Existing scheduling vendors are crowded.
Optimization must not create access inequity.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong optimization and interaction-design fit with comparatively lower clinical risk.

evidence.title: AMA: technology to cut no-shows and save practice time
evidence.note: AMA practice guidance describes patient-engagement technology as a way to reduce no-shows and staff burden.

evidence.title: AMA EHR workflow research
evidence.note: Workflow design is a measurable contributor to physician efficiency and burnout.

opportunities.title: Clinical-time leakage diagnostic
opportunities.wedge: Measure where physician and staff time disappears across documentation, authorization, inbox, scheduling and handoffs, then rank interventions by recovered clinical capacity.
opportunities.buyer: Practice owner, medical group COO or service-line leader.
opportunities.painMoment: Everyone says they are overloaded, but we cannot see which administrative system is actually consuming the clinical day.
opportunities.firstTest: Time-map one practice for two weeks and sell the intervention roadmap before building software.
riskNotes: Needs staff trust and access to operational data.
Diagnosis may reveal organizational rather than software problems.
opportunities.fitNote: Very strong diagnostic/service-design entry wedge before taking on clinical software risk.

evidence.title: AMA prior authorization time burden
evidence.note: One administrative workflow alone consumes an average 13 hours per physician/staff team weekly.

evidence.title: AMA EHR use research
evidence.note: Audit-log and transaction data can identify workflows that detract from care and efficiency.

opportunities.title: Skill + crew capacity orchestration
opportunities.wedge: Match project-phase demand, certified skills, crew availability and geographic constraints before labor shortages become schedule delays.
opportunities.buyer: General contractors and specialty subcontractors.
opportunities.painMoment: We won the work, but the right people are not available when the schedule says we need them.
opportunities.firstTest: Forecast labor gaps across three live projects for one contractor and compare with actual staffing shortages.
riskNotes: Workforce data quality can be weak.
Union/certification rules vary.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong scheduling/system-design fit, moderate domain-learning requirement.

evidence.title: AGC 2026 workforce shortage survey
evidence.note: AGC reports workforce shortages remain the top reason for construction project delays.

evidence.title: AIA 2026 staffing conditions
evidence.note: Adjacent AEC staffing data also shows recruiting remains difficult across design teams.

opportunities.title: Field evidence + change-order capture
opportunities.wedge: Turn photos, daily logs, RFIs, instructions and schedule impacts into a defensible real-time change record before commercial memory diverges.
opportunities.buyer: GC project teams and subcontractors.
opportunities.painMoment: Everybody knows the work changed, but weeks later nobody agrees who asked, what it cost, or whether notice was given.
opportunities.firstTest: Instrument one project and compare discovered change events with formally captured change orders.
riskNotes: Contract notice rules differ.
Evidence must remain tamper-resistant and attributable.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent multimodal evidence, workflow and AI-synthesis fit.

evidence.title: AIA construction-administration AI guidance
evidence.note: AEC administration contains heavy information-management work around RFIs, submittals and professional decisions.

evidence.title: AIA fee and scope guidance
evidence.note: Scope, risk and project conditions are central to managing compensated professional services.

opportunities.title: Permit + preconstruction dependency preflight
opportunities.wedge: Map permits, inspections, utility dependencies, long-lead approvals and responsible parties before the committed schedule becomes fiction.
opportunities.buyer: Small and mid-size contractors, owners and developers.
opportunities.painMoment: The crew is ready, but one approval or dependency nobody owned has stopped the project.
opportunities.firstTest: Run a manual dependency preflight on five projects before notice-to-proceed and track avoided delays.
riskNotes: Requirements are jurisdiction-specific.
Professional permitting advice boundaries vary.
opportunities.fitNote: Direct service-design and rules/orchestration fit.

evidence.title: AGC workforce and delay context 2026
evidence.note: Project delays remain a central contractor problem, with labor shortages a leading cause.

evidence.title: AIA 2026 regulatory and delay concerns
evidence.note: Architecture firms cite regulatory/environmental issues and cancelled/delayed/redesigned projects among business concerns.

opportunities.title: Subcontractor execution-risk radar
opportunities.wedge: Combine staffing, submittals, schedule adherence, safety signals and commercial issues into an explainable early-warning view.
opportunities.buyer: General contractors and construction managers.
opportunities.painMoment: By the time a subcontractor is visibly failing, the recovery schedule is already expensive.
opportunities.firstTest: Score subcontractor risk on completed projects retrospectively, then prospectively on one live job.
riskNotes: Risk scoring can damage vendor relationships.
Must avoid opaque or discriminatory scoring.
opportunities.fitNote: Good analytical/product fit with strong governance requirement.

evidence.title: AGC 2026 workforce survey
evidence.note: Skill shortages and labor availability are material execution risks across contractors.

evidence.title: AIA project benchmark tracking
evidence.note: AEC firms already track project hours, budgets and cost benchmarks, showing available operational signals.

opportunities.title: Progress billing + pay-app evidence checker
opportunities.wedge: Reconcile percent complete, field evidence, schedule values, lien requirements and change status before payment applications move.
opportunities.buyer: Owners, GCs and subcontractors.
opportunities.painMoment: Cash flow depends on a pay application that crosses project controls, accounting and field reality.
opportunities.firstTest: Human-review one monthly billing cycle and measure discrepancies caught before submission.
riskNotes: Accounting and contract rules vary.
Source documentation must be authoritative.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong document reconciliation and workflow UX fit.

evidence.title: AIA construction administration information burden
evidence.note: Construction administration is heavily driven by document and information coordination.

evidence.title: AGC 2026 project delay context
evidence.note: Tight project conditions amplify the cost of administrative and execution delays.

opportunities.title: Margin-leak diagnostic
opportunities.wedge: Decompose food, labor, delivery, discounts, waste and menu mix to show the few controllable leaks actually destroying restaurant profit.
opportunities.buyer: Independent restaurant owner or small group operator.
opportunities.painMoment: Sales look okay, but there is almost nothing left at the end of the month.
opportunities.firstTest: Analyze 90 days of POS, payroll and purchasing data for five restaurants and charge only for a ranked action plan.
riskNotes: POS/accounting integrations vary.
Operators may have little cash despite high pain.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent diagnostic/data product fit with rapid measurable outcomes.

evidence.title: National Restaurant Association: elevated costs pressure profitability
evidence.note: Total restaurant expenses are 36% above pre-pandemic levels, keeping margins under pressure.

evidence.title: 2026 State of the Restaurant Industry
evidence.note: Operators identify rising costs, uneven traffic, technology and productivity as central 2026 issues.

opportunities.title: Labor scheduling + staffing ROI planner
opportunities.wedge: Forecast demand and schedule enough skill coverage without turning understaffing or unnecessary labor into margin loss.
opportunities.buyer: Restaurant managers and multi-unit operators.
opportunities.painMoment: One bad schedule either destroys service or wipes out the day's profit.
opportunities.firstTest: Run four weeks of shadow scheduling against actual sales and labor outcomes in one location.
riskNotes: Crowded scheduling-software market.
Local labor rules must be modeled correctly.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong forecasting/UX fit with excellent feedback loops.

evidence.title: National Restaurant Association workforce research
evidence.note: Staffing decisions have measurable ROI, with costs from understaffing, turnover and new-hire ramp time.

evidence.title: Restaurant job openings September 2026
evidence.note: Hospitality labor demand cooled but staffing remains a core operational variable.

opportunities.title: Purchasing + menu engineering copilot
opportunities.wedge: Connect ingredient costs, recipes, waste, supplier substitutions and item profitability so menu decisions react before margins disappear.
opportunities.buyer: Chef-owner, F&B director or restaurant group finance lead.
opportunities.painMoment: Ingredient cost changed again, but the menu price and prep system still assume last quarter.
opportunities.firstTest: Track 20 high-volume ingredients and 30 menu items for one restaurant; quantify recovered gross margin.
riskNotes: Recipe and inventory data is often messy.
Supplier systems can be fragmented.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong data synthesis and operational decision-support fit.

evidence.title: Restaurant cost pressure analysis
evidence.note: Food commodities and other operating expenses remain elevated, making productivity and cost management critical.

evidence.title: 2026 restaurant industry report
evidence.note: Operators are investing in automation and data analytics to improve efficiency.

opportunities.title: Opening + recurring compliance command center
opportunities.wedge: Convert permits, inspections, licenses, renewals and required records into one location-specific operating calendar.
opportunities.buyer: Independent restaurant founder or small chain.
opportunities.painMoment: A permit nobody owned can delay opening while rent and payroll continue.
opportunities.firstTest: Manually build the complete compliance graph for five new restaurants in one city.
riskNotes: Rules are hyperlocal.
Must distinguish operational guidance from legal advice.
opportunities.fitNote: Excellent rule-orchestration and service-design fit.

evidence.title: 2026 restaurant industry report
evidence.note: Restaurant operators continue facing a challenging cost and operations environment.

evidence.title: National Restaurant Association staffing research
evidence.note: Operational stability is tightly linked to execution systems, staffing and technology.

opportunities.title: Demand + prep waste optimizer
opportunities.wedge: Forecast by daypart and item, then convert uncertainty into prep ranges rather than one brittle demand number.
opportunities.buyer: Restaurant operators with meaningful perishables and variable traffic.
opportunities.painMoment: We either run out during the rush or throw tomorrow's margin in the bin tonight.
opportunities.firstTest: Shadow forecast ten perishable items for four weeks and measure waste plus stockouts.
riskNotes: Many POS vendors already offer basic forecasting.
Value depends on measurable waste data.
opportunities.fitNote: Strong analytics product with exceptionally fast experimentation.

evidence.title: National Restaurant Association 2026 industry report
evidence.note: Uneven traffic and productivity pressure remain major operator concerns.

evidence.title: Restaurant profitability cost analysis
evidence.note: Elevated input costs increase the value of reducing controllable waste.
